fun_fact: With only a few dozen birds left at its low point, it is one of the rarest birds on Earth, but numbers are now rising.
clue: Once down to a few dozen birds, this black flycatcher clings on in a few lowland valleys.

why_here: It grows only on the high Temehani plateaus of Raiatea.
fun_fact: Its fan-shaped white flower looks like half a flower, and over-collecting plus rats have made it critically endangered.
clue: Its fan-shaped white flower looks like half a flower, on a high, misty volcanic plateau.

why_here: Black rats wiped it out on the other Marquesas islands, but Ua Huka has never had black rats.
fun_fact: Its deep blue plumage makes it one of the most striking parrots in the Pacific.
clue: A deep-blue parrot that survives only on one rugged volcanic isle black rats never reached.

place: Western valleys of Nuku Hiva, Marquesas
why_here: Hunting and habitat loss left it only in remote western valleys of Nuku Hiva.
fun_fact: At about 900 g it is one of the largest tree-dwelling pigeons in the world.
clue: At about 900 g, one of the world's biggest tree-dwelling pigeons, in remote volcanic gorges.

why_here: This flightless black rail evolved on one remote, uninhabited raised coral island.
fun_fact: Its population crashed after a failed rat eradication in 2011 but recovered within four years.
clue: A flightless black rail of an empty raised coral island. It recovered after a failed rat purge.

why_here: It evolved on uninhabited Henderson Island and is the only one of the island's four endemic pigeons still alive.
fun_fact: Henderson once had four endemic pigeon species; this is the only one that survives.
clue: The last survivor of four pigeon species found only on its uninhabited raised coral island.

why_here: Brown tree snakes wiped it out on Guam, leaving snake-free Rota as its last refuge.
fun_fact: The last native crow on Guam disappeared in 2011.
clue: Invasive tree snakes wiped it off a nearby island; one snake-free tropical isle is its haven.

why_here: It evolved on the Raja Ampat islands off New Guinea and never crossed to the mainland.
fun_fact: Males have two long, twisted ribbon-like tail wires, and take about six years to grow their full red plumes.
clue: Males grow two twisted, ribbon-like tail wires, taking about six years to get full plumage.

why_here: It is restricted to the hill forests of two Raja Ampat islands.
fun_fact: Males have a bare turquoise-blue crown with a black cross pattern and two curled tail feathers; Attenborough first filmed it in 1996.
clue: Males have a bare turquoise crown crossed in black and two curled tail feathers.

place: Ayamaru Lakes, Bird's Head, West Papua
why_here: It evolved in one isolated mountain lake system on the Bird's Head Peninsula.
fun_fact: Half blue and half orange, it is a hugely popular aquarium fish, and wild collecting has threatened the lake population.
clue: Half blue, half orange: an aquarium hit, and wild collecting threatens its one mountain lake.

why_here: It lives only in the isolated, almost untouched cloud forests of the Foja Mountains.
fun_fact: Known only from trade skins for nearly a century, its home was finally found by Jared Diamond in 1981; males build tower bowers decorated with fruit.
clue: Males build tower bowers decorated with fruit in untouched cloud forest, found only in 1981.

why_here: This egg-laying mammal survives only in the Cyclops Mountains, a small coastal range that is hard to reach.
fun_fact: Unrecorded for over 60 years, it was caught on a trail camera in 2023.
clue: An egg-laying mammal unrecorded for over 60 years, until a trail camera caught it in 2023.

why_here: It lives only in mossy montane forest along the summits of the Torricelli range, covering no more than about 125 km2.
fun_fact: Local villages agreed to stop hunting it, and it is considered perhaps the most intelligent tree-kangaroo.
clue: A kangaroo that lives in trees, in cold, mossy cloud forest on a tropical ridge.

why_here: It evolved in one isolated highland lake that has over a dozen fish species found nowhere else.
fun_fact: Also called the turquoise rainbowfish for its glowing blue body.
clue: A glowing turquoise fish from one highland lake with over a dozen fish found nowhere else.

why_here: It lives only in the cloud forests of the rugged Huon Peninsula.
fun_fact: Its pregnancy lasts about 44 days, unusually long for a marsupial; it may have been carried to nearby Umboi Island by people.
clue: Its pregnancy lasts about 44 days, long for a marsupial, in cold, rugged cloud forest.

why_here: This bird-of-paradise lives west of New Guinea, only on the forested North Moluccan islands.
fun_fact: Males raise four long white plumes from their wings like flags while displaying; Wallace's assistant Ali first collected it.
clue: Males raise four long white plumes from their wings like flags while displaying.

why_here: It is known only from three North Moluccan islands, where it nests inside active termite mounds.
fun_fact: It is the world's largest bee, with a wingspan of about 6 cm, and was rediscovered in 1981 after being thought extinct.
clue: The world's largest bee, with a wingspan of about 6 cm, nests inside active termite mounds.
